After the movers leave,
I find one blue cup
behind the stove.
At dusk, the empty room
holds one square of warmth.
I leave the cup on the sill,
a small address for morning.

artifacts.text:
Your coat keeps its shoulder-shape
beside the unlit door.
I blame the road that took you,
then remember how you mocked its dust.
I will not call this loss a lesson.
Still, I mend the loosened button
and hang the coat where morning reaches it.
contexts: Complete elegy. Revision note: the unlit-door image is conventional, while lament, protest, memory, refusal, and care form a coherent movement.

Leave the light on, you said,
while rain erased the steps.

Leave the light on—
not an order now,
but proof I had delayed too long.

At dawn I leave the light on
for whoever still believes
this house can open.

The station clock forgets a minute.
I keep your ticket in my sleeve.
Rain threads silver through the platform.
The northbound doors refuse to close.

I keep your ticket in my sleeve—
now proof that leaving had a price.

the conductor waits for me to choose.

Now proof that leaving had a price,
I step aboard without goodbye.
The conductor waits for me to choose.
Your empty seat receives the rain.
